title: Counterexamples to additivity of minimum output $p$-Rényi entropy of quantum channels for $p>3/4$ and $0\leq p<1/4$
authors: Debbie Leung, Benjamin Lovitz, Peixue Wu
abstract: Additivity of minimum output entropies is a central problem in quantum information theory. Nonadditivity is known for every Rényi order $p>1$, at the von Neumann point $p=1$, and near $p=0$, while most of the interval $0<p<1$ has remained open. We prove that for every Rényi order $p$ satisfying either $p>3/4$ or $0\leq p<1/4$, there exist finite-dimensional projection-induced quantum channels such that additivity of the minimum output $p$-Rényi entropy fails. The proof combines two correlated random-projection constructions: a product-conjugate Bell-state witness for $p>3/4$, and a transpose-complement rank-defect witness for $p<1/4$. Thus the unresolved part of $0<p<1$ is reduced to $[1/4,3/4]$. Our estimates also improve the output dimension threshold for additivity violation of minimum output von Neumann entropy, first established in Belinschi, Collins and Nechida.
summary: This paper tackles the long-standing problem of additivity for minimum output $p$-Rényi entropy of quantum channels. By constructing explicit counterexamples using random projections, the authors prove nonadditivity holds for large ranges of the Rényi order parameter $p$, thereby significantly constraining the remaining unknown regime to $[1/4, 3/4]$. This advances the theoretical understanding of entanglement measures in quantum information theory.
main_problem: The central problem is determining the additivity of the minimum output $p$-Rényi entropy ($	ext{S}_{\min}^p(\Phi)$) for quantum channels, which asks if $	ext{S}_{\min}^p(\Phi \otimes\Psi) = 	ext{S}_{\min}^p(\Phi) + 	ext{S}_{\min}^p(\Psi)$.
main_result: The authors prove that additivity fails for all Rényi orders $p$ in the ranges $[0, 1/4) \cup (3/4, \infty)$, significantly narrowing the unresolved interval to $[1/4, 3/4]$.
method: The proof employs sophisticated random-projection constructions and asymptotic analysis, utilizing specific witnesses (product–conjugate Bell-state witness for $p>3/4$ and transpose-complement rank-defect witness for $p<1/4$).
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum channels ($\Phi$) acting on finite-dimensional systems, specifically those induced by Haar-distributed projections ($P_{AB,n}$) on a bipartite system.
key_observables: Minimum output $p$-Rényi entropy ($	ext{S}_{\min}^p(\Phi)$), and the limiting one-channel output body $K_{k,t}$.
important_parameters: The Rényi order parameter $p$, and the asymptotic rank ratio parameter $t \in (0, 1)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on establishing the almost sure convergence of the actual output set $	ext{C}_n$ to a theoretical limit $K_{k,t}$ as system size $n 	o \infty$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the additivity failure by constructing explicit counterexamples for specific ranges of $p$, combining random-projection techniques with asymptotic entropy calculations.
why_interesting: This work provides deep theoretical insights into fundamental properties of quantum information measures, which are crucial for understanding channel capacity and entanglement quantification in open quantum systems.
